text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Deficit now three times higher than projected. Finance Minister Lino Spiteri told parliament on Monday night that the soaring budget deficit had been the reason behind the former prime minister's decision to call early elections. Spiteri did not give figures, but the previous government had budgeted a deficit of Lm31 million ($90 million).

- Malta left out of Euro Banknotes map. The designer of the new European currency, Robert Kalina, 41 of Austria, has apologised for leaving Malta, Cyprus and the Isle of Wight out of a map of Europe to be carried at the back of new banknotes. The ommission, pointed out by British Prime Mnister John Major in Dublin last week, is to be corrected.
- Audit report on Roads Department shows work orders worth Lm10 million ($28 million) have been given over-budget and without finance ministry approval.

- The government agency Management Systems Unit ended the contract of foreign consultant Tony Walshe after he refused to have a Maltese understudy. Walshe had been praised in a report on the MSU presented to the prime minister last month.
- Anger at government decision to stop fast catamaran service to Gozo. The service to the sister island, introduced just before the October 26 elections, was stopped because it was unprofitable.
